title: Feature: Axonometric Grid Support
author: allandiegoasilva
body:
# Feature Proposal: Axonometric Grid Support

## Description

Hi everyone!

I'd like to contribute to VectorCraft by proposing support for an **axonometric grid**, similar to the one available in Inkscape.

This type of grid is useful for creating isometric illustrations, 3D-style icons, architectural drawings, and other vector artwork.

## Proposed Feature

The idea is to introduce an axonometric grid with the following capabilities:

- Configurable grid spacing and angles.
- Support for isometric and other axonometric grid configurations.
- Optional snapping to grid intersections to make drawing and alignment easier.
- Integration with the existing grid settings and drawing workflow.

## Default Behavior

I'd also like to discuss whether the axonometric grid should be enabled by default or remain an optional grid that users can enable when needed.

I'm open to whichever approach best fits VectorCraft's design philosophy and existing architecture.

## Questions

1. Would this feature be a good fit for VectorCraft?
2. Is anyone already working on something similar?
3. Would the maintainers be open to a contribution implementing this functionality?

I'd be happy to work on the implementation if the proposal aligns with the project's direction.

Thanks for your time!

title: SVG import: <textPath> pointing at a basic shape (circle, rect, …) imports as point type
author: switch87
body:
## What

SVG 2 lets `<textPath href="#id">` point at any basic shape (`circle`, `ellipse`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`), not only at a `<path>`. VectorCraft 0.9.0 only follows a `<path>`. For a basic shape it imports the text as point type and warns:

```
textPath has no usable path; imported as point type
```

Inkscape writes exactly this as soon as you put text on a circle, so it is common in real files (for example ring texts around a round logo).

## Repro

`tp.svg`:
```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" width="300" height="300" viewBox="0 0 300 300">
  <circle id="c1" cx="150" cy="150" r="100" fill="none" stroke="#ccc"/>
  <path id="p1" d="M50 150 A100 100 0 0 1 250 150" fill="none"/>
  <text font-size="20"><textPath xlink:href="#c1">TEXT ON A CIRCLE</textPath></text>
  <text font-size="20"><textPath xlink:href="#p1">TEXT ON A PATH</textPath></text>
</svg>
```

- `vectorcraft-cli info tp.svg`: the warning above, for the circle.
- `vectorcraft-cli convert tp.svg out.png`: only "TEXT ON A PATH" is drawn on its path.

## Expected

The basic shape is converted to its equivalent path, as SVG 2 defines it (*Shapes › equivalent path*), and the text runs along it. For a circle or ellipse the path starts at 3 o'clock (cx + rx, cy) and runs clockwise. For a rect it starts at (x + rx, y) and runs clockwise, and for line, polyline and polygon it follows the points in order. The shape's own `transform` applies as it does for a `<path>`.

I'm working on this.

title: Linux: fontconfig-listed TeX Gyre font under /usr/share/texmf is missing and falls back to Source Sans 3
author: excited-raccoon
body:
## Problem

On Linux, VectorCraft 0.10.0 does not discover the installed **TeX Gyre Bonum Bold** face under `/usr/share/texmf/fonts/opentype/public/tex-gyre/`, although fontconfig lists it. Requesting that family/style through `vectorcraft-cli` succeeds in creating text, but the text resolves to **Source Sans 3 Bold** instead.

An explicit `text.rescanFonts` does not fix the missing family. Other installed fonts, such as **URW Bookman Demi**, resolve exactly in the same environment.

## Environment

- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, x86_64
- VectorCraft Debian package: `vectorcraft 0.10.0-1`
- Installed font package: `fonts-texgyre 20180621-7`
- Font file: `/usr/share/texmf/fonts/opentype/public/tex-gyre/texgyrebonum-bold.otf`
- Reproduced with the headless CLI, both with and without MCP automation filesystem roots
- No fonts were installed or downloaded for this test

## Reproduction

Confirm the font is installed and visible to fontconfig:

```bash
fc-list | rg -F '/usr/share/texmf/fonts/opentype/public/tex-gyre/texgyrebonum-bold.otf'
```

Output:

```text
/usr/share/texmf/fonts/opentype/public/tex-gyre/texgyrebonum-bold.otf: TeX Gyre Bonum:style=Bold
```

In a fresh CLI session, create text using that family/style and check its resolution:

```bash

title: Export: a raster effect (blur, shadow, glow, grain) drawn after a pattern fill comes out tiny and displaced
author: switch87
body:
## What

When an object with a raster live effect (Gaussian Blur, Drop Shadow, Outer/Inner Glow, Grain, …) is drawn **after** an object with a **pattern fill**, the effect's raster comes out tiny and displaced in PNG/TIFF/WebP export and `vectorcraft-cli convert`. The preview and PDF are right. Tested on `main` (0.10.0, `bd9b8a2d`) and 0.9.0.

## Repro (MCP, headless)

1. `file.new` 300×200.
2. Make a pattern from a small dot (`object.pattern.make`), then fill an 80×80 rectangle at (10, 10) with it.
3. Draw a grey 70×70 ellipse at (225, 115) and apply `blur.gaussian` to it.
4. Export PNG: the blurred circle is a small dot at a different place. The centre of the circle is transparent in the TIFF, PNG (144 ppi) and WebP exports.

## Cause

`pattern::set_pattern_paint` (`crates/render/src/pattern.rs`) sets a **paint transform** on the context (`xf * scale(1/sx, 1/sy)`) and leaves it set. Solid colours ignore paint transforms, so nothing else notices. But `fx.rs` draws its rasters as image paints, in `draw_scaled` (blurs and other raster effects) and in the shadow/glow path. Those set the geometry transform and not the paint transform, so they sample their pixmap through the pattern's leftover scale. The same happens after a radial or freeform gradient, which also set a paint transform.

I'm working on this.

title: PDF/EPS import: a clip whose bounding box covers the page is dropped, even when it is a diamond or circle
author: switch87
body:
## What

PDF and EPS import leave out a clipping path that "covers the page". But they decide that from its **bounding box** alone: any path of at most 6 straight segments whose box contains the page is treated as redundant. A diamond (or any polygon) whose corners touch the page edges has the page as its box, so its clip is dropped, and everything it should cut away shows. Tested on `main` (0.10.0) and 0.9.0, with both an EPS and an Inkscape-written PDF of an orange square clipped to a diamond that touches the page edges: VectorCraft shows the full square.

- PDF: `push_clip_path` in `crates/pdf/src/import.rs` (`redundant`).
- EPS: `Interp::clip` in `crates/eps/src/import/graphics.rs`.

## Expected

The clip is only skipped when it really covers the page, meaning it is a convex polygon that contains all four page corners. Otherwise it is kept.

I'm working on this.

title: PDF import: an alpha soft mask drawn as an image (Inkscape/cairo) comes in empty
author: switch87
body:
## What

A soft mask with `/S /Alpha` takes its values from the **alpha** of its art. The PDF import handles that for vector art by whitening it (`import_mask::whiten`, which keeps the opacity), but not for **images**. cairo, and so Inkscape, writes a mask as a group that draws an image whose alpha is in its own `/SMask`. That image keeps its colour (often black), so the mask's luminance comes out as the image's colour instead of its alpha. With black pixels the mask is empty and the masked object disappears. Tested on `main` (0.10.0) and 0.9.0 with an Inkscape PDF of a red square under a white-to-black gradient mask: only a hairline is left.

I'm working on this.

title: EPS/PS import: Type 42 fonts (cairo, Inkscape, LibreOffice) come in 1000× too large
author: switch87
body:
## What

PostScript and EPS files from cairo (and so Inkscape), LibreOffice and others embed TrueType as **Type 42** fonts. Their text comes in 1000× too large, far off the page, so it seems to disappear. Tested on `main` (0.10.0) and 0.9.0 with a cairo EPS saying "Hi".

## Cause

`Interp::font` (`crates/eps/src/import/text.rs`) turns the font's `FontMatrix` into the matrix of a one-unit em as `FontMatrix × 1000`. That holds for Type 1 fonts, whose glyphs are in 1000-unit space (`FontMatrix [0.001 0 0 0.001 0 0]`). But a Type 42 font's glyph space is normalised to one unit per em (PLRM / Adobe TN 5012). Its `FontMatrix` is usually the identity and is itself the em matrix.

I'm working on this.

title: SVG import: absolute units inside a drawing (1in, 25.4mm, 72pt) don't match its unitless lengths
author: switch87
body:
## What

In SVG, user units are CSS pixels and absolute lengths convert at 96 px per inch, so inside one drawing `width="1in"` is exactly as wide as `width="96"`. VectorCraft's SVG import (M4.18, `RootUnits` in `crates/svg/src/import.rs`) passes usvg a dpi of **72** when the root `width`/`height` have no absolute unit, so that a pixel is a point and `1in` is 72 pt. The result is that mixed lengths no longer fit together. Repro on `main` (0.10.0):

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="200" height="100" viewBox="0 0 200 100">
  <rect x="0"   y="0"  width="96"     height="50" fill="red"/>
  <rect x="0"   y="50" width="1in"    height="50" fill="blue"/>
  <rect x="100" y="0"  width="72pt"   height="50" fill="green"/>
  <rect x="100" y="50" width="25.4mm" height="50" fill="orange"/>
</svg>
```

Browsers, rsvg and Inkscape draw all four 96 wide. VectorCraft draws the blue, green and orange ones 72 wide, so the layout breaks: gaps and misaligned edges in any file that mixes units, which Inkscape does for `stroke-width` and font sizes, for example.

## Possible fixes

This is a trade-off between the drawing's own geometry and physical sizes, so I'd like your call before writing it:

1. **Convert at 96 everywhere** (what the spec requires), and keep the "px = pt" scale for the whole drawing, so `1in` comes out as 96 pt. The geometry is always right, but a `font-size="12pt"` inside a unitless drawing becomes 16 pt, the same as in a browser at that scale.
2. Keep 72 for the root size only. Inside the drawing, convert absolute lengths at 96 and scale the whole drawing by 0.75 when the root is unitless. That keeps physical sizes, but changes the size of today's unitless imports.

I'm happy to implement whichever you prefer.

title: SVG import: CSS transform drops the element's transform, the font shorthand is ignored for text, :not() never matches
author: switch87
body:
## What

Three CSS gaps in SVG import, tested on `main` (0.10.0):

1. **`transform` as a CSS property** (in `style` or a `<style>` rule) with CSS syntax, such as `transform: translate(100px, 100px)` or `rotate(45deg)`. usvg takes `transform` as a presentation attribute that overrides the element's `transform` attribute, but svgtypes can't parse CSS units, so the element ends up with **no transform at all**. A `<rect transform="translate(0 100)" style="transform: translate(100px, 0)">` lands at (0, 0) instead of (100, 0), and a rect moved only by CSS stays at its origin.
2. **The `font` shorthand** (`style="font: italic bold 30px 'DejaVu Sans'"`) on text is ignored: the text comes in at the default size and weight. usvg expands it, but VectorCraft's own text pass (`import/css.rs`) doesn't.
3. **`:not()`** selectors never match. `rect:not(.keep){fill:green}` leaves the rect red. The selector matching is simplecss's, so this one may be out of scope here.

I'm working on 1 and 2.

title: SVG import: percentage lengths in <symbol> use the <use> viewport instead of the symbol viewBox
author: excited-raccoon
body:
Percentage lengths in a referenced `<symbol viewBox="0 0 100 100">` are imported using the `<use>` element's width/height (260×180) as the percentage basis, then scaled by the viewBox transform. This silently enlarges and displaces the symbol's artwork.

## Reproduction

VectorCraft / vectorcraft-cli 0.10.0, Linux x86_64. Save the following as `symbol-percent.svg`:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"
     width="440" height="300" viewBox="0 0 440 300">
  <rect width="440" height="300" fill="#fff2cc"/>
  <defs>
    <symbol id="icon" viewBox="0 0 100 100">
      <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="#e63946"/>
      <circle cx="50%" cy="50%" r="35%" fill="#457b9d"/>
    </symbol>
  </defs>
  <use xlink:href="#icon" x="50" y="40" width="260" height="180"/>
</svg>
```

Run:

```sh
vectorcraft-cli run --in symbol-percent.svg \
  --cmd document.inspect --params '{"depth":5}' \
  --export actual.png
```

Opening the SVG reports `warnings: []`.

## Expected

The symbol's percentage lengths resolve in its 100×100 viewBox: the rectangle is 100×100, and the circle has center (50,50) and radius 35. With the default `xMidYMid meet` transform, the visible result is a red 180×180 square at (90,40), with a centered blue circle at (180,130), radius 63.

This follows [SVG's percentage-unit rules](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/coords.html#Units). It is also verified with librsvg 2.61.3: the percentage fixture renders pixel-identically to a control fixture replacing the rectangle dimensions with `100`, and the circle's `cx`, `cy`, `r` with `50`, `50`, `35`. VectorCraft imports that numeric control with the expected appearance.

## Actual

The percentage fixture shows a wider red rectangle and a large blue circular segment at the bottom/right, instead of the centered circle. `document.inspect` reports:

- Red rectangle: x=90, y=40, width≈468, height≈324 (expected 180×180).
- Blue circle bounds: x≈183.128, y≈61.128, width=height≈28…

## Expected

`<flowRoot>` with a rectangle region comes in as **area type**: the rectangle is the frame, each `<flowPara>` is a paragraph, and the style comes from the cascade as for `<text>`. Any other region gets at least a warning.

I'm working on this.

title: Commands that take ids? refuse with "nothing selected" when the objects are given but none is selected
author: switch87
body:
## What

Many commands document `ids?` (operate on these objects; default: the selection), for example `object.repeat.radial`, `object.envelope.makeWithWarp`, `object.pattern.make`, `symbol.new`, `path.join` and `edit.colors.invert`. With objects given in `ids` but nothing selected, they fail with **"nothing selected"** before they run: `Session::execute` checks the command's `enabled` predicate, which looks at the selection, and only `edit.clear` makes an exception for `ids`. Scripts and MCP agents that name their targets, rather than selecting them first, can't use these commands.

On `main` (0.10.0) I swept every command whose description mentions `ids`, with one rectangle given and nothing selected: **48** were refused this way. Their `run` already uses the `ids`. With the gate fixed, all of them run on the given object or fail for a real reason (not text, not an open path, too small for the grid…).

## Proposal

When a command's description takes `ids` and they are given, evaluate its `enabled` **as if those objects were selected**, then put the selection back. Each predicate keeps its meaning (for example, Make with Top Object still needs two objects); it just sees the given objects.

I'm working on this.

title: Arc warp ignores the object's aspect ratio: skewed sides from 10 %, the inner edge folds over at 100 %
author: switch87
body:
## What

The **Arc** warp style (envelope `object.envelope.makeWithWarp` and the Warp effect) works on box coordinates normalised to −1..1 on **both** axes (`warp_point` in `crates/doc/src/live.rs`). It bends the centre line into a circular arc whose radius is in x units but offsets the edges in y units, so for any object that isn't square the result is no circular arc. For a wide, low object (a text banner, say):
- from Bend 10 % the sides lean in and the shape looks skewed rather than bent;
- at 100 % the radius (2/π) is smaller than the half-height (1 in y units), so the inner edge **folds over** past the centre.

Tested on `main` (0.10.0): a 300 × 80 rectangle with Arc at 10, 25, 50 and 100 %.

## Expected

The arc is round in the object's real proportions: the centre line keeps its length on a circular arc (sweep = Bend × 180°), and the top and bottom edges are concentric arcs at their real distance from it. An inner edge that would pass the centre stops there instead of folding.

I'm working on this.

title: Exported JPEG/TIFF/PSD carry an sRGB ICC profile whose tags aren't 4-byte aligned (634 bytes)
author: switch87
body:
## What

The ICC profiles VectorCraft writes (`cms::icc::encode`, used for embedded profiles in JPEG, TIFF and PSD exports) are made by `moxcms`'s `ColorProfile::encode`. moxcms doesn't pad tag data to 4 bytes. On `main` (0.10.0) the built-in sRGB profile is **634 bytes**: its `desc` tag (`mluc`, 62 bytes) is followed by `cprt` at offset **558**, which isn't a multiple of 4. ICC.1 §7.1.2 requires every tagged element to start on a 4-byte boundary, with padding, so the profile size is a multiple of 4. Stricter readers reject such a profile or the whole file (the report this came from: ImageMagick refused the files in its setup).

```
tag   offset size
desc  496    62    mluc
cprt  558    76    mluc   ← unaligned
```

## Fix

After encoding, lay the tag data out again with each element padded to 4 bytes, and update the tag offsets and the header's size (tags that share data keep sharing it). I'll also report it to moxcms.

I'm working on this.

title: Opening an SVG by a bare file name doesn't find its relatively linked images
author: switch87
body:
## What

`document.open {"path": "linked-image.svg"}` (or `vectorcraft-cli info/convert linked-image.svg` run in its folder) with an `<image href="ext.png">` next to it warns `linked image 'ext.png' not found` and puts in a placeholder. The same file opened by its absolute path finds the image. Tested on `main` (0.10.0).

The SVG's folder for relative links comes from `Path::parent()` of the name, which is `""` for a bare file name. `load_with` filters that empty folder out, so there is no folder at all. Because the placeholder's link then holds the bare `ext.png`, `links::resolve` (relative to the process's working directory) finds the file again and doesn't list it in `missingLinks` either, so the result contradicts its own warning.

## Expected

A relative `path` is the file in the working directory: its folder is that directory, and relative links resolve from it, exactly as for the absolute path.

I'm working on this.

title: Area type in a non-rectangular shape breaks a word in the middle when the top lines are too narrow for it
author: switch87
body:
## What

Area type in a shape that is narrow at the top (a triangle, a circle) breaks the first words letter by letter where they don't fit, without a hyphen: "Wonderful extraordinary typesetting" in a triangle comes out as `Wo / nderful / extraordina / ry typesetting`. Tested on 0.9.0, and the code on `main` (0.10.0) is the same.

## Cause

`Pen::place` (`crates/text/src/layout.rs`) accepts a line once its span is wider than about the ascent (`fits`). `break_line` then has to fit the next word into it and, finding no break opportunity, breaks inside the word (the greedy overflow at the end of `break_line`). The Every-line Composer's simulation (`compose_para`, `sim.place`) takes the same line widths.

## Expected

In area type, a line too short for the next word stays empty and the word moves down to where the shape is wide enough. Only a word wider than every line still in the frame is broken (or hyphenated, with Hyphenation on).

## A way to do it

Give `place` the width of the next unbreakable word (glyph advances up to the first break opportunity) as a minimum span width, for non-rectangular regions only (rectangles have one width, so nothing better exists below). Try a cloned `Pen` with that minimum, and fall back to today's call when no line in the region is wide enough. `compose_para` needs the same rule when it collects its line widths, or it would place lines where the greedy pass doesn't.

title: Roughen (Smooth): turn-backs become cusps, PDF viewers draw miter spikes there
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this.

## What

With **Roughen** (Smooth points) on a stroked path, PDF export shows long spikes in MuPDF, poppler (pdftoppm, Okular) and, smaller, Ghostscript. VectorCraft's own preview and PNG export, and cairo, don't show them. It is the same in 0.10.0 and on `main`.

Repro: a 5-point star (radius 70/32, no fill, 10 pt stroke), Roughen `size 3, detail 10` as an appearance effect, exported to PDF with `preserveEditing: false`.

## Why

Roughen jitters the resampled points by more than their spacing, so now and then a point lands *behind* its predecessor and the path turns back. `catmull_rom` (`crates/effects/src/util.rs`) makes each anchor's handles from `next − prev`. At such a turn-back, `next ≈ prev`, so the handles shrink to (almost) nothing. The anchor becomes a cusp whose two directions point nearly the same way.

In the repro, the anchor at (80.3, 82.1) has 0.36 pt handles against 6.7 pt chords. Renderers that join at that cusp draw a miter up to the limit of 10: a spike of 10 × half the stroke width. The preview's stroker doesn't, so the export doesn't match what's on screen.

## Proposed fix

When `next − prev` is short compared with the chords to the neighbours (a sharp turn), point the handles along the bisector of the two chords: `normalize(u + v)`, or the perpendicular of `u` for an exact reversal. Keep them collinear, with at least the length a regular turn would get. The turn then becomes a round hairpin with a continuous tangent, and every renderer draws it the same.

Regular turns keep exactly the current tangents, so other uses of `catmull_rom` (Zig Zag, Scribble) and the existing render goldens don't change.

title: rfc: Establish minimum quality standards for AI agents & discourage blind PR rushing
author: reyhe66243

AI agents can be extremely valuable for open-source maintenance when used properly, but their effectiveness depends entirely on *how* they engage with the codebase and the community. 

Right now, we are seeing two opposite extremes in this repository:

### Why blind PR rushing hurts the project

A full Rust-based vector design suite is a deeply complex project. Features, shortcuts, rendering pipelines, and UX patterns cannot simply be patched blindly.

title: Scribble: on concave shapes the zig-zag crosses the holes between spans
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this.

## What

**Scribble** on a concave shape draws lines outside the shape. On a 5-point star (fill only), the rows through the two legs run straight across the gap between them, and the rows through the arms run across the notches.

## Why

`scribble` (`crates/effects/src/stylize.rs`) collects each row's spans, the inside intervals of the scanline, and chains *all* of them into one polyline: the end of one span is joined to the start of the next. When a row has more than one span, that join crosses the hole between them.

## Proposed fix

Chain spans per region instead. A span continues the zig-zag whose previous row's span it overlaps; a span that overlaps none starts a new zig-zag (a subpath of its own). Where a region splits, one side continues and the other starts. Where two regions merge, one of them ends.

Convex shapes have one span per row, so their result stays exactly the same.

title: EPS import: a stitched shading loses its hard colour change at a bound
author: switch87
body:
I'm working on this; the PR follows right away.

## What

An EPS/PS shading whose function is a stitching function (`FunctionType 3`) with pieces that don't meet at a bound loses the hard colour change there. The PDF reader keeps it.

```postscript
0 0 200 50 rectclip
<< /ShadingType 2 /ColorSpace /DeviceRGB /Coords [0 0 200 0]
   /Function << /FunctionType 3 /Domain [0 1] /Bounds [0.5] /Encode [0 1 0 1]
     /Functions [ << /FunctionType 2 /Domain [0 1] /C0 [1 0 0] /C1 [0 0 1] /N 1 >>
                  << /FunctionType 2 /Domain [0 1] /C0 [1 0 0] /C1 [0 0 1] /N 1 >> ] >> >> shfill
```

| | stops |
|---|---|
| expected (red → blue, then red → blue again) | 0 red, 0.5 blue, 0.5 red, 1 blue |
| 0.10.0 and `main` | 0 red, 0.5 red, 1 blue: the left half is a flat red |

## Why

`crates/eps/src/import/graphics.rs` turns each bound of a stitched linear function into one stop, evaluated at the bound itself. That is the right piece's colour, so the left piece's end colour is lost.

title: Save failures can be silent when the destination is locked or unavailable
author: fryrow
body:
## Summary

When saving a document fails because the destination file is locked or otherwise unavailable, VectorCraft can fail without showing a persistent error message. The status message is transient and is easy to miss; background-save failures have the same problem.

## Reproduction

1. Open or create a document.
2. Save it to a file.
3. Lock the destination file or otherwise remove write access (for example, hold an exclusive lock from another application).
4. Modify the document and save again.

## Observed

The save does not complete, but no visible error dialog explains the failure.

## Expected

Show a persistent error message that saving failed, include the destination and underlying reason when available, and leave the document marked as unsaved/dirty so the user can retry or choose another path.

## Environment

Windows desktop build of VectorCraft from `storytold/vectorcraft`.

title: [Vectorcraft] UX issue: field order while changing colour values numerically
author: 2CLC
body:
### AI Color Picker behavior
In AI, you can use TAB to switch between color values in the color picker dialog. When you hit TAB, cursor jumps to the next value from the same color mode, be it RGB, HSB, CMYK, or to the HEX#.

### VectorCraft's current Color Picker behavior
In VC, you can do the same, but the cursor jumps from value to value across the color modes and especially when you want to jump from CMYK Y value to CMYK K value, in between it jumps to the HEX# that is not updated yet, which changes all the colors back to the value HEX# had while jumped on its value. Jumping one TAB next to the CMYK K value then changes all the CMYK colours.

**See attached videos to visualize the issue.**

### Expected VC behavior

author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). This is an AI-assisted, read-only source audit: the failure scenario was **not runtime-reproduced**, no exploit payload was developed, and no destructive test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/package.rs:316-338](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/package.rs#L316-L338): root is `Path::new(folder).join(name)`; validation checks name syntax, not overlap. Root entry uses the source stem plus `.vectorcraft` and contains a relinked clone.
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/package.rs:358-365](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/package.rs#L358-L365): generated entries are written with replacing write_file calls.

## Conditions and impact
For a saved native source, choosing folder/name whose joined path is its current parent directory makes the packaged native entry equal the source path. Packaging overwrites the original with the relinked package version while the live source document remains unchanged. Existing linked-file destinations can also collide. This is accidental destructive output overlap, not a privilege-escalation claim.

## Recommended remediation
Resolve output/source identities and reject collisions with the source or dependencies. Prefer a new package directory and non-replacing writes; validate every destination before publishing any file.

## Suggested regression coverage
Package a synthetic native document into its source parent and require rejection with byte-identical source/dependencies. Cover path aliases, an existing package directory, and an ordinary separate destination.

title: [Audit] Native streaming open does not bound skipped or replayed decompression work
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). This is an AI-assisted, read-only source audit: the failure scenario was **not runtime-reproduced**, no exploit payload was developed, and no destructive test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [crates/format/src/unpack.rs:140-161](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/format/src/unpack.rs#L140-L161): the budget sums requested lengths, not offsets or total decoder work.
- [crates/format/src/unpack.rs:186-207](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/format/src/unpack.rs#L186-L207): skip inflates to a sink without a cumulative budget; overlapping references restart the gzip decoder and skip the JSON prefix again.

## Conditions and impact
A tiny requested blob at a distant offset causes all preceding decoded data to be discarded, outside the retained-length budget. Repeated overlapping references restart the decoder and replay the prefix; sorting offsets does not prevent equal/overlapping references. A compact compressed file can therefore cause disproportionate CPU work despite small retained blobs. This is distinct from missing in-memory copy accounting: the streaming retained-length checks are present.

## Recommended remediation
Bound accepted extents and cumulative decoded work, including discarded bytes and every replay. Resolve shared/overlapping intervals in one bounded pass or charge/reject replay explicitly.

## Suggested regression coverage
With a small instrumented work budget, test a tiny blob beyond an oversized gap and overlapping references after a modest prefix. Require bounded rejection, plus successful contiguous and below-budget shared-reference cases.

title: [Audit] PDF embedded-editing name-tree search revisits shared Kids exponentially
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). This is an AI-assisted, read-only source audit: the failure scenario was **not runtime-reproduced**, no exploit payload was developed, and no destructive test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [crates/pdf/src/editing.rs:94-108](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/pdf/src/editing.rs#L94-L108): recursive `Kids.iter::<Dict>().find_map(|kid| editing_spec(&kid, depth + 1))` has a depth limit but no total visit count or memoized completed nodes.
- [crates/pdf/src/editing.rs:76-80](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/pdf/src/editing.rs#L76-L80): ordinary editing-data discovery calls it.

## Conditions and impact
An acyclic chain of indirect name-tree dictionaries can repeat the next dictionary in each Kids array. When no matching attachment exists, all occurrences are explored. Work grows as branching factor raised to depth despite only a small number of stored dictionaries; MAX_DEPTH 16 does not adequately bound it. Hayro’s ancestor-cycle guards do exist, but do not prevent repeated acyclic DAG traversal.

## Recommended remediation
Track visited/completed indirect node identities and enforce a total search budget for nodes and Names entries, while retaining depth protection.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use an original tiny PDF with a valid page tree and shared acyclic Kids. With a small traversal budget or visit instrumentation, assert bounded termination and correct discovery in a shared subtree containing a legitimate attachment.

title: [Audit] SVG descendant-selector matching can perform combinatorial ancestor backtracking
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). This is an AI-assisted, read-only source audit: the failure scenario was **not runtime-reproduced**, no exploit payload was developed, and no destructive test was run.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [crates/svg/src/import/css.rs:167-182](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/svg/src/import/css.rs#L167-L182): each descendant component recursively tries every matching ancestor: `ancestors().skip(1)...any(|a| go(rest, a))`.
- [crates/svg/src/import/css.rs:266-292](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/svg/src/import/css.rs#L266-L292): the declaration cache does not memoize selector-suffix/node states.
- [crates/svg/src/import/text.rs:258](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/svg/src/import/text.rs#L258): the text importer constructs this Styles matcher.

## Conditions and impact
A nested SVG whose ancestor classes match repeated descendant selector components, but whose leftmost selector component cannot match, makes the matcher exhaust ancestor combinations before returning false. Compact selector/tree input can stall import. Existing #1557 discusses different CSS semantic gaps; this report is about matcher work complexity, not :not() support.

## Recommended remediation
Memoize (selector suffix, node) matching states or use a bounded non-backtracking matcher, plus per-document work/selector-length limits.

## Suggested regression coverage
Import modest nested groups with text and a descendant rule whose leftmost class is absent. Assert bounded state visits under an injected budget; include successful matching and mixed child/descendant controls.

- [crates/affinity/src/raster.rs:108-110](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/affinity/src/raster.rs#L108-L110): pixel limits apply per image only.

- [crates/affinity/src/raster.rs:245-254](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/affinity/src/raster.rs#L245-L254): channel planes are allocated independently; constant tile states need no archive tile bytes.

## Conditions and impact
Many individually valid sparse/constant-state raster layers allocate channel planes and retained RGBA output while extracting little archive data. The archive max_total counter and model node cap therefore do not bound aggregate generated-pixel memory, allowing import memory exhaustion. This is not a claim that archive decompression has no limits.

## Recommended remediation
Carry a reader-wide decoded/generated-memory budget, charging retained outputs and simultaneously live channel/temporary buffers before allocation.

## Suggested regression coverage
Build an original small synthetic Affinity container with several constant-state ras…

title: [Audit] Stacked Transform effects expand geometry without an aggregate allocation/work budget
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/effects/src/distort.rs:130-143](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/effects/src/distort.rs#L130-L143) clamps copies to 1000, but every iteration appends all subpaths of the transformed input. [crates/effects/src/lib.rs:751-766](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/effects/src/lib.rs#L751-L766) feeds each visible geometry effect’s whole output into the next; Transform dispatch is at line 783.

## Conditions and impact
Identity Transform copies remain inside the coordinate-reach guard, so each stage multiplies subpath count by copies + 1. Stacking allowed effects produces multiplicative geometry growth from a small document. There is no shared anchor/subpath/byte/work budget before cloning. Renderer cache budgets govern retained results, not expansion. Rendering or baking can stall or exhaust memory and lose unsaved work.

## Recommended remediation
Enforce a shared checked geometry budget across the stack, including input complexity and prospective output before cloning. Return a recoverable failure or explicitly documented bounded fallback.

## Suggested regression coverage
Under a small test budget, evaluate stacked identity transforms through apply_geometry_with and require bounded rejection. Include detailed input and a permitted small stack; never allocate production-scale oversized results.

title: [Audit] Shadow/glow fallback bypasses raster budgets and can allocate a 65535-square surface
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/render/src/fx.rs:580-582](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/render/src/fx.rs#L580-L582) rejects cached shadows above 8192 per side or 4 million pixels. [crates/render/src/fx.rs:859-874](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/render/src/fx.rs#L859-L874) falls through to with_filters; Inner Glow also calls it at 893–895. [crates/render/src/fx.rs:1234-1252](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/render/src/fx.rs#L1234-L1252) inflates art and viewport by blur/pixel size, caps each dimension at u16::MAX without area validation, then allocates offscreen_context and Pixmap. [crates/effects/src/raster.rs:105-125](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/effects/src/raster.rs#L105-L125) permits blur up to 1000 pt.

## Conditions and impact
In multithreaded rendering, large blur at high zoom reaches the fallback. At 32× zoom and 1000 pt blur, spread is 48,002 device pixels per side, allowing 65535 × 65535 output even for a modest viewport. One RGBA surface is about 16 GiB before intermediates. Bounded content-filter planning at fx.rs:953–964 does not cover this shadow/glow fallback. This can stall or terminate the editor.

## Recommended remediation
Apply a preallocation area/byte budget including intermediates. Use correctly scaled lower-resolution filtering or bounded overlapping tiles; rejection by the shadow cache must not cause a larger unbudgeted allocation.

## Suggested regression coverage
Test region plannin…

title: [Audit] Scatter horizontal tick generation can fail to terminate after finite arithmetic overflows
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/graph.rs:252-258](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/graph.rs#L252-L258) rounds axis endpoints without checking result finiteness. [crates/engine/src/cmd/graph.rs:264-289](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/graph.rs#L264-L289) provides finite value_axis and bounded tick_values alternatives, but [crates/engine/src/cmd/graph.rs:893-900](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/graph.rs#L893-L900) bypasses them for scatter X, appending art while `x <= xh + xs * 1e-6` and incrementing `x += xs`.

## Conditions and impact
Finite scatter X data near the maximum finite float can yield finite positive step but infinite rounded high endpoint. Eventually x becomes infinity, stops changing, and the condition remains true. Generation keeps appending art. Finite-input checks cannot prevent derived overflow; validation after generation is too late.

## Recommended remediation
Use a validated horizontal axis and bounded counted tick generation, as for the value axis. Require finite endpoints/span and progression.

## Suggested regression coverage
Exercise graph.create and graph.setData with finite data whose rounded high overflows, using bounded test execution. Require bounded geometry or controlled error; include ordinary and near-boundary valid controls.

title: [Audit] Liquify MAX_DABS is checked before, not during, segment expansion
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/tools/src/distort/liquify.rs:327-343](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/tools/src/distort/liquify.rs#L327-L343) checks MAX_DABS once before a loop appending while `s <= len`; the precheck uses > instead of >=. [crates/engine/src/cmd/distortcmds.rs:603-608](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/distortcmds.rs#L603-L608) accepts finite coordinates without a distance budget; [crates/engine/src/cmd/distortcmds.rs:620-626](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/distortcmds.rs#L620-L626) extends the stroke before result application.

## Conditions and impact
One long segment can exceed the advertised 20,000-dab cap by any practical amount. Very large finite endpoints can produce infinite distance or an accumulator that stops progressing. The UI can hang or exhaust memory before geometry validation. Checking between segments cannot protect one segment.

## Recommended remediation
Enforce a cap on every append path, including held dabs; validate derived distance and use a checked bounded count instead of unchecked floating accumulation.

## Suggested regression coverage
With a small test cap, a long finite segment/small brush must keep public Dabber output bounded and object.liquify must complete. Cover exactly-at-cap, held dabs and derived nonfinite distance without huge allocations.

title: [Audit] Control ui.drag steps and ui.click count expand synthetic events without bounds
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:212-238](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L212-L238) accepts arbitrary u64 steps and count, then appends events in `1..=steps` and `1..count` loops. [apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs:108-121](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs#L108-L121) bounds request-line bytes but not numeric expansion.

## Conditions and impact
A tiny valid request on the enabled loopback control channel can demand effectively unbounded UI-thread work and allocation. count also applies to drag. A buggy automation client can freeze/terminate the editor and lose unsaved work. This is within intended local automation, not Internet exposure or an authentication bypass.

## Recommended remediation
Validate both counts against explicit small maxima before appending any events, plus a total synthetic-event budget per request/frame.

## Suggested regression coverage
Reject just-over-limit and u64::MAX values without queue mutation. Verify boundary values and normal clicks/drags; do not generate resource-exhausting queues.

title: [Audit] Upgrade reachable ruzstd 0.9.0: RUSTSEC-2026-0344 decompression memory exhaustion
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** High. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[Cargo.lock:3642-3648](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/Cargo.lock#L3642-L3648) pins ruzstd 0.9.0. Untrusted input reaches StreamingDecoder::new_with_max_window_size in [crates/affinity/src/container.rs:313-328](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/affinity/src/container.rs#L313-L328) and [crates/eps/src/import/ai/mod.rs:138-160](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/ai/mod.rs#L138-L160). [RUSTSEC-2026-0344](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0344.html), independently returned by OSV for this lockfile, identifies missing per-block decompressed-size enforcement, fixed in 0.9.1.

## Conditions and impact
The vulnerable dependency is reachable in document import. Existing window and outer take/read_bounded limits are real safeguards but cannot prevent internal block allocation before output reaches the caller. The advisory describes memory exhaustion and a related counter panic, not corruption or code execution. Lock version and reachability are source-confirmed; no crafted compressed input was executed.

## Recommended remediation
Update resolved ruzstd to at least 0.9.1 or a newer compatible fixed release. Retain outer limits and enforce dependency-advisory checking in CI.

## Suggested regression coverage
Rerun lockfile auditing and existing Affinity/EPS import/fuzz suites after updating. Verify native/WASM compatibility and bounded invalid-block metadata handling with safe upstream regression coverage.

title: [Audit] Unix atomic-save staging exposes private document contents before permissions are preserved
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/format/src/atomic.rs:30-31](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/format/src/atomic.rs#L30-L31) creates adjacent staging with create_new but no private Unix mode. [crates/format/src/atomic.rs:55-68](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/format/src/atomic.rs#L55-L68) writes/flushed contents before keep_permissions; permissions are copied at [crates/format/src/atomic.rs:225-229](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/format/src/atomic.rs#L225-L229). The system-temp fallback already uses 0600 at [crates/format/src/atomic.rs:98-104](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/format/src/atomic.rs#L98-L104).

## Conditions and impact
On Unix, replacing a 0600 document in a directory another user can traverse under a typical 022 umask creates a temporarily 0644 copy. Another user can open staging before chmod and retain that descriptor afterward; interruption can leave readable staging behind. create_new prevents following an existing staging symlink, and private parent directories prevent disclosure. Windows ACL exposure is not established.

## Recommended remediation
Create adjacent staging mode 0600 from the outset; apply intended final permissions immediately before publication and define a policy for new files.

## Suggested regression coverage
Inspect staging permissions inside write_atomic_with’s fill callback while replacing a 0600 target under umask 022. Require owner-only staging and preserved final permiss…

title: [Audit] Export for Screens suffix can escape the selected output folder
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/screens.rs:170-174](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/screens.rs#L170-L174) copies custom suffix verbatim. [crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/screens.rs:355-357](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/screens.rs#L355-L357) incorporates it into the relative filename. [crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/screens.rs:304-310](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/screens.rs#L304-L310) creates derived parents and writes the resulting path.

## Conditions and impact
Separators and parent components in suffix turn the prefixed stem into an intermediate directory followed by traversal. Output can leave the selected export folder and replace existing files. Automation root checks still apply: this does not demonstrate escape from configured write roots. Ordinary unconfined use and other destinations inside an authorized root remain affected.

## Recommended remediation
Reject separator/path/control syntax in suffixes and validate generated names as single filename components. Retain independent automation-root confinement.

## Suggested regression coverage
Call document.exportForScreens with traversal-bearing suffixes and reject before creating directories or writing. Cover both separator styles, valid custom suffixes and confined-root controls.

title: [Audit] EPS interpreter leaks cyclic arrays and dictionaries after import
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/eps/src/import/obj.rs:12-15](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/obj.rs#L12-L15) and [crates/eps/src/import/obj.rs:138-146](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/obj.rs#L138-L146) use strong Rc composite storage. Put writes objects directly at [crates/eps/src/import/interp.rs:888-900](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/interp.rs#L888-L900). release at [crates/eps/src/import/interp.rs:200-208](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/interp.rs#L200-L208) clears standard roots/stacks/journal, not every allocated composite. Normal/error import invokes it at [crates/eps/src/import/mod.rs:195-196](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/mod.rs#L195-L196).

## Conditions and impact
PostScript can create self/mutually referential arrays and dictionaries. Dropping roots does not break their internal strong cycles, including composites abandoned earlier. Retained memory accumulates across imports; per-run work/memory budgets do not reclaim it. This is a leak, not memory unsafety.

## Recommended remediation
Use interpreter-owned handle/arena storage or register all allocated composites so teardown can break every edge. Traversing only current roots misses abandoned cycles.

Use tiny self-array/dictionary, mutual/mixed and abandoned cycles. Verify recla…

title: [Audit] EPS ASCII85 decoding allocates before output and interpreter-memory budget checks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/eps/src/ps.rs:185-211](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/ps.rs#L185-L211) appends without an output cap; z emits four bytes. ASCII85Decode calls it at [crates/eps/src/import/data.rs:268-272](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/data.rs#L268-L272); materialize decodes before self.alloc at [crates/eps/src/import/data.rs:619-626](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/data.rs#L619-L626). Literals also use it at [crates/eps/src/import/lex.rs:242-246](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/lex.rs#L242-L246).

## Conditions and impact
Expansion-heavy/large encoded input can exceed the 256 MiB filter policy before 1 GiB interpreter accounting notices. Source/intermediate buffers can coexist. This is linear expansion (up to four bytes per z), not arbitrary compression ratio. ATE already pre-bounds encoded size; AI editing input is capped but permits a large intermediate. Flate/LZW limits do not repair this path.

## Recommended remediation
Pass remaining output/memory budgets into ASCII85 and check before reserve/append. Budget source copies and simultaneously live filter stages before materializing them.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use tiny injected budgets with z, ordinary/partial groups, whitespace, literals and chained filters. Require preallocation rejection and positive below-budget controls.

title: [Audit] Compressed DIB validates bitmap dimensions only after decode and RGBA conversion
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/metafile/src/dib.rs:163-169](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/metafile/src/dib.rs#L163-L169) calls image::load_from_memory(...).to_rgba8 before checking side/pixel limits. EMF/WMF callers at [crates/metafile/src/import/emf.rs:81-84](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/metafile/src/import/emf.rs#L81-L84) and [crates/metafile/src/import/wmf.rs:145-155](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/metafile/src/import/wmf.rs#L145-L155) validate record boundaries, not decoded dimensions.

## Conditions and impact
An over-limit compressed bitmap is fully decoded and converted before rejection. Low-channel input can expand considerably as RGBA. image has a default 512 MiB decoder allowance: decoding is not unlimited, but that allowance does not enforce the metafile’s stricter dimensions before work or jointly budget RGBA conversion.

## Recommended remediation
Read compressed-payload dimensions first, configure decoder limits and budget decoded storage plus conversion. Do not trust wrapper dimensions alone.

## Suggested regression coverage
With lowered budgets, reject excessive PNG/JPEG dimensions before full decode; cover misleading DIB wrappers, grayscale-to-RGBA expansion and valid controls.

title: [Audit] Image sampling, recolouring, and link proxies lack conversion-aware working-memory budgets
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/doc/src/pixels.rs:23-25](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/doc/src/pixels.rs#L23-L25) decodes/converts before recolouring and allocating its RGB memo. [crates/doc/src/pixels.rs:62-71](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/doc/src/pixels.rs#L62-L71) converts and caches sampling RGBA. [crates/doc/src/links.rs:125-132](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/doc/src/links.rs#L125-L132) reads dimensions only to decide if a proxy is needed, then decodes fully. [crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/load.rs:425-441](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/load.rs#L425-L441) stores common encoded formats after header inspection, so the new engine decoder allowance does not protect these later operations.

## Conditions and impact
Large encoded images can load successfully but cause excessive working memory during sampling, recolouring or proxy generation. image’s default decoder limit exists but does not jointly bound decoder storage, RGBA conversion, retained cache, memo and output. Grayscale can expand fourfold as RGBA. The RGB memo is finitely bounded by the colour space, not literally infinite. Process failure depends on available memory, especially on WASM.

## Recommended remediation
Use a fallible shared decode/conversion helper with predecode dimension and combined working-memory checks. Budget retained caches, intermediates and recolouring memoization.

title: [Audit] Native document ID exhaustion survives loading and breaks later node, artboard, and style creation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/doc/src/lib.rs:771-788](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L771-L788) saturates the recovered next_id at u64::MAX but alloc_id then executes unchecked `self.next_id += 1`. [crates/format/src/lib.rs:544](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/format/src/lib.rs#L544) calls fix_next_id without rejecting exhaustion. Artboard IDs use max + 1 at [crates/doc/src/lib.rs:1369-1370](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L1369-L1370); style IDs at [crates/doc/src/lib.rs:1453-1459](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L1453-L1459). Style lookup excludes zero at line 1450.

## Conditions and impact
Native JSON can supply maximum IDs or an exhausted next_id. Overflow-checked builds panic on the next allocation; unchecked release arithmetic wraps, risking reused node IDs. Artboard/style max remains present, so repeated allocations can return zero; zero styles are not addressable through normal lookup. Panic guards may report an internal error on native, but do not repair the file; WASM panic handling differs. The newer ID index handles some existing duplicates but does not make allocation safe.

## Recommended remediation
Use checked fallible ID allocation or normalize hostile IDs/counters at load while consistently rewriting references. Saturating allocation is not a fix because it repeats IDs; preserve reserved zero semantics.

title: [Audit] Redo during a live interaction leaves a stale cancel/preview baseline
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs:288-302](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs#L288-L302) swaps document/history without settling or rebasing the interaction. [crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:176-177](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs#L176-L177) enables redo from history alone. Subsequent preview restores it.doc at [crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1571-1573](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L1571-L1573); cancellation restores it at [crates/engine/src/lib.rs:463-471](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L463-L471).

## Conditions and impact
With redo history available, begin a live interaction, then redo. A subsequent preview or cancel restores the pre-redo baseline while history still records the redo. This unexpectedly loses the redone edit and makes history inconsistent with the document.

## Recommended remediation
Settle/cancel the interaction before redo, reject redo while interacting, or rebase both history and interaction consistently.

## Suggested regression coverage
Create/edit/undo, begin a drag, redo, then separately preview and cancel. Assert document plus undo/redo stacks obey the chosen semantics.

title: [Audit] Failed live previews are still recorded as committed journal commands
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1578-1584](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L1578-L1584) saves the execute Result, then assigns it.preview regardless of failure. [crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1590-1601](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L1590-L1601) takes that preview at commit; line 1619 appends it to the journal.

## Conditions and impact
An invalid or disabled preview returns an error but a later commit journals the failed command. A failing second preview also replaces the previous successful recorded preview after resetting the document. Replay/actions can fail or diverge from the committed document.

## Recommended remediation
Update commit-ready preview/journal state only after success, and explicitly define whether a failed second preview preserves or resets the previous successful state.

## Suggested regression coverage
Begin an interaction, submit a failing preview, commit, and assert no failed journal entry/spurious history. Repeat after a successful preview and verify state/journal consistency.

title: [Audit] Save planning mutates live file dates before validation or writing succeeds
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs:422-430](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs#L422-L430) stamps live dates before job_for. Native/artboard/preset validation can fail at [crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs:447-453](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs#L447-L453); later encoding/writing can fail at [crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs:621-634](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs#L621-L634).

## Conditions and impact
Save/Save As with a destination and timestamp changes live created/modified metadata before any successful write. Invalid options or an I/O error leaves dates changed and can affect pointer-based dirty tracking despite no successful save. This is a separate state-mutation defect from #1685’s error presentation.

## Recommended remediation
Stamp an isolated save snapshot and publish appropriate live metadata only after successful completion, respecting edits made while a background save runs.

## Suggested regression coverage
Inject writer failure through save_with and exercise invalid encoding options. Require unchanged live dates, document and dirty status. Include successful save with intervening-edit controls.

title: [Audit] Automatic linked-file updates during a drag are discarded but their new stamps remain acknowledged
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/engine/src/link_watch.rs:118-144](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/link_watch.rs#L118-L144) records the new stamp, then executes links.update without deferring an active interaction. [crates/engine/src/lib.rs:1571-1573](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L1571-L1573) resets art to the interaction snapshot on the next preview; cancellation restores the same baseline at 463–471. Desktop completed scans are applied at [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:830-831](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L830-L831).

## Conditions and impact
A watched file changes during a drag. The automatic update applies to the preview state, then the next preview/cancel discards it. Its new stamp stays recorded, so later scans see no change and do not retry. Committing immediately instead folds the update into the drag rather than preserving it as an independent change.

## Recommended remediation
Defer applying and acknowledging updates until interactions settle, or explicitly rebase and journal independent background changes.

## Suggested regression coverage
Using public link-scan/apply APIs with synthetic linked art, detect a change during preview and then preview/cancel/commit. Require the update to survive independently or remain pending for retry.

title: [Audit] Pattern tile caching ignores changes to referenced symbols and nested resources
author: PierrunoYT
body:

**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High (source-level).

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

[crates/render/src/pattern.rs:35-61](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/render/src/pattern.rs#L35-L61) stores direct art/tiling and a thread-local cache; same_art compares direct Arc identities. [crates/render/src/pattern.rs:160-166](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/render/src/pattern.rs#L160-L166) validates only direct art/params/scale while tile rendering at [crates/render/src/pattern.rs:98-108](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/render/src/pattern.rs#L98-L108) reads the current document. title: [Audit] 3D solid effects replace NonZero compound-path fill semantics with nesting parity
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/effects/src/solids.rs:197-215](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/effects/src/solids.rs#L197-L215) receives FillRule but does not pass it to fill facets. [crates/three-d/src/solid.rs:322-334](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/three-d/src/solid.rs#L322-L334) labels every oddly nested ring as a hole and rewrites its direction. Extrude, Rotate and Inflate call rings at solid.rs:635,671,1002, without a fill-rule parameter.

## Conditions and impact
Two nested same-winding contours under NonZero fill have a filled centre (winding magnitude two), but rings reverses the inner contour into a hole. Even a zero-rotation unshaded Rotate can remove filled area; Extrude/Inflate likewise derive the wrong solid. Baked/expanded art can retain this incorrect geometry. This concerns ordinary valid compound paths, not only malformed intersections.

## Recommended remediation
Carry FillRule through the solid API and normalize the actual filled region before constructing caps/walls. NonZero requires winding accumulation, not nesting parity alone; remove contours that are not material boundaries.

## Suggested regression coverage
Apply zero-rotation unshaded Rotate through solid_art to same-winding nested NonZero rectangles and require a filled centre/preserved area. Opposite-winding NonZero and same-winding EvenOdd controls must retain holes. Extend controls to Extrude caps and Inflate.

title: [Audit] Control requests can execute after their caller has received a timeout
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs:59-66](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs#L59-L66) sends a request, then returns timeout after 60 seconds without cancellation. [crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:37-47](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L37-L47) carries method/params/reply only. [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:735-750](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L735-L750) executes every drained request before attempting reply delivery.

## Conditions and impact
If UI draining is delayed beyond 60 seconds, the caller receives timeout but the queued edit remains executable. When UI processing resumes it can apply unexpectedly; a caller retry can duplicate it. The request queue is unbounded. Remote’s old automatic replay bug is already fixed and is not the cause here. Intended exposure is enabled loopback automation, not a public service.

## Recommended remediation
Give queued requests deadline/cancellation state checked before execution and bound the queue. Distinguish expiry before start from an operation already started whose outcome is unknown.

## Suggested regression coverage
With a short injected deadline, enqueue a harmless edit while draining is paused, expire it, resume draining and assert no edit. Separately test timeout after execution begins and report uncertainty rather than promising cancellation.

title: [Audit] Idle control sockets can occupy all connection slots indefinitely
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs:40-65](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs#L40-L65) caps active connections at 16 but sets no socket read/write timeout. [apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs:108-121](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs#L108-L121) caps line bytes, not time; reply writes at [apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs:148-156](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/apps/vectorcraft/src/control_server.rs#L148-L156) are synchronous without deadlines.

## Conditions and impact
Sixteen idle or partial-line loopback clients retain every slot indefinitely, denying legitimate automation. A peer that stops reading a sufficiently large reply can retain a worker too. The response-channel timeout does not time out socket reads/writes. This does not itself demonstrate UI freezing or Internet exposure.

## Recommended remediation
Set checked read/write deadlines and an absolute line-completion deadline so trickled bytes cannot keep slots indefinitely. Release worker/connection accounting on timeout.

## Suggested regression coverage
With short configurable deadlines, verify idle and partial-line clients release slots and a nonreading peer cannot retain a worker indefinitely. Ensure normal persistent clients still work.

title: [Audit] MCP framing and batch processing lack byte, work, and accumulated-result limits
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/mcp/src/server.rs:82-115](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/mcp/src/server.rs#L82-L115) uses input.lines(), parses entire batches, collects every reply, then serializes a complete String without an application cap. [crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:68-72](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L68-L72) reads remote replies into an unbounded String. [crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:918-961](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/mcp/src/tools.rs#L918-L961) places no maximum on command_batch steps and retains both result values and response records.

## Conditions and impact
A faulty/untrusted integration can cause large line allocations, long sequential batches and accumulated responses. A custom/faulty remote endpoint can return an arbitrarily long line. Nesting limits do not cap line length or array width; read timeouts do not impose byte limits. MCP is stdio and Remote normally uses loopback; this is not a claim of public unauthenticated network exposure. Not every tool yields disproportionate output from a tiny input.

Bound lines before parsing, both batch forms before dispatch, remote replies and aggregate output/results. Use pagination/export for legitimately large responses and checked remote write timeouts.
