title: [Audit] MCP accepts invalid JSON-RPC versions and Remote accepts mismatched response IDs
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[crates/mcp/src/server.rs:119-138](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/mcp/src/server.rs#L119-L138) validates method/id shape but never requires jsonrpc == "2.0" before dispatch/notifications. [crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:78-89](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L78-L89) generates a request ID but accepts the reply based only on ok/result/error, without correlation.

## Conditions and impact
Missing/wrong-version request envelopes can invoke tools or change notification state. A faulty/custom endpoint can make Remote attribute an unsolicited or mismatched result to the current call. These are protocol correctness defects, not authorization bypasses. The standard desktop server echoes IDs and Remote now drops its connection after I/O failure, so the fixed automatic-replay scenario must not be used to inflate impact.

## Recommended remediation
Validate JSON-RPC version before any request/notification dispatch. Require exact outstanding response ID in Remote and reject/discard mismatched or malformed responses.

## Suggested regression coverage
Wrong/missing-version mutating requests must return Invalid Request with zero backend calls; malformed initialized notifications must not change state. A mock endpoint returning missing/wrong ID must never be accepted as success.

title: [Audit] PngSuite corpus downloader extracts unauthenticated HTTP content without digest verification
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[xtask/src/main.rs:227](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/xtask/src/main.rs#L227) defines a plain HTTP archive URL. [xtask/src/main.rs:252-258](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/xtask/src/main.rs#L252-L258) downloads with curl -fsSL and immediately runs tar -xzf, without expected digest. Lines 260–262 validate success by counting .png entries only.

## Conditions and impact
A network intermediary controlling the HTTP response for the opt-in cargo xtask corpus --download command can substitute corpus data that is extracted and accepted. This permits test-oracle substitution and extraction disk consumption. No tar directory-escape or code-execution claim is made. The separate Affinity downloader already uses pinned HTTPS sources and digest verification and is not affected by this specific issue.

## Recommended remediation
Pin/verify a reviewed SHA-256 digest before extraction and prefer HTTPS. Bound download/extraction sizes and allow only intended regular corpus entries.

## Suggested regression coverage
A substituted archive containing a .png filename must fail digest verification before extraction. Cover oversized input and unexpected entry types; verify the pinned valid corpus succeeds.

title: [Audit] Track unmaintained rustybuzz and ttf-parser dependencies reported by RustSec
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low (maintenance; not a confirmed vulnerability). **Confidence:** High for the stated source/dependency facts.

Reviewed upstream main at [0d0ea352](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/commit/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0). AI-assisted read-only source audit: **not runtime-reproduced**; no exploit payload or destructive test.

## Root cause and source evidence
[Cargo.lock:3624-3639](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/Cargo.lock#L3624-L3639) locks rustybuzz 0.20.1; [Cargo.lock:4306-4313](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/Cargo.lock#L4306-L4313) locks ttf-parser 0.25.1. Lockfile dependency edges are krilla 0.8.2 → rustybuzz → ttf-parser. An OSV query of all 564 registry package/version entries returned [RUSTSEC-2026-0206](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0206.html) and [RUSTSEC-2026-0192](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0192.html), both explicitly informational/unmaintained.

## Conditions and impact
These crates remain in the resolved dependency graph but upstream maintainers have stopped fixes. This creates maintenance/security-response risk over time; neither advisory establishes an exploitable defect in these versions. Do not classify these notices as equivalent to the active ruzstd advisory reported separately.

## Recommended remediation
Track a compatible krilla/dependency update that removes the unmaintained chain, or document a reviewed maintenance plan. Advisory-listed alternatives include harfrust for shaping and skrifa for font parsing; avoid swapping algorithms without output validation.

## Suggested regression coverage
After any migration, verify shaping, font subsetting/PDF export, representative scripts and malformed-font handling plus native/WASM builds. Rerun advisory scanning and ensure notices disappear for the intended reason.

title: Native save/reopen changes live warped text inside a symbol
author: excited-raccoon
body:
A symbol containing live point type inside a Wave envelope changes its rendered glyph contours after saving to `.vectorcraft` and reopening in a fresh process. The same envelope outside a symbol round-trips unchanged. This makes a saved editable logo/wordmark look different when reopened.

## Minimal reproduction

Uses the bundled Source Sans 3 font. No rotation, reflection, duplication, cross-document paste or external artwork is needed.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
repro_dir="$(mktemp -d -t vectorcraft-symbol-envelope-XXXXXX)"
vectorcraft-cli run \
  --cmd file.new --params '{"width":600,"height":300,"colorMode":"rgb"}' \
  --cmd text.create --params '{"x":30,"y":160,"text":"STUDIO","size":72,"font":"Source Sans 3","color":"#E3AB49"}' \
  --cmd text.fonts \
  --cmd object.envelope.makeWithWarp --params '{"style":"wave","bend":18}' \
  --cmd symbol.new --params '{"name":"Master"}' \
  --cmd document.save --params "{\"path\":\"$repro_dir/document.vectorcraft\"}" \
  --export "$repro_dir/before.png" --scale 2 > "$repro_dir/create.jsonl"
vectorcraft-cli convert "$repro_dir/document.vectorcraft" "$repro_dir/after.png" --scale 2 \
  > "$repro_dir/reopen.jsonl"
printf '%s\n' "$repro_dir"
```

Compare `before.png` with `after.png` in the printed directory. Both are 1200 × 600. The warped letters change contour/position when the native file is reopened; this is visible around the tops and bottoms of the letters.

## Expected

Reopening a native file should retain the same live envelope/symbol appearance. No text, warp parameters, instance transform, font or artboard setting changed.

## Observed and controls

- All commands, save and reopen succeed. Save/export report no warnings.
- `text.fonts` reports Source Sans 3 Regular with `status: exact`, `missing: false`, and zero missing glyphs.

title: Arrow keys don't work in the search / command palette
author: delit
body:
## Summary

The search function (opened from the magnifier icon in the top bar) shows a list of matching commands, but the **arrow keys cannot be used to move through the results**. The list can only be used with the mouse, which breaks the keyboard-only workflow that a command search is meant to support.

## Current behavior

- Open the search from the magnifier icon in the top bar (see screenshot 2).
- Type a query, for example `Artboard`. A list of matching commands appears (see screenshot 1).
- The first result is highlighted (blue), but pressing **Up Arrow** / **Down Arrow** does **not** move the selection to other results.
- The only way to pick another result is to hover or click it with the mouse.

## Expected behavior

| Key | Expected result |
|---|---|
| **Down Arrow** | Move the selection to the next result |
| **Up Arrow** | Move the selection to the previous result |
| **Enter** | Run the selected command |
| **Esc** | Close the search |

Additional details:

- The highlighted result should scroll into view if the list is longer than the visible area.
- Navigation should wrap around (optional): Down on the last result goes to the first, and Up on the first goes to the last.
- Keyboard selection and mouse hover should not conflict. The most recent input (key or mouse) decides which result is highlighted.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Vectorcraft.
2. Click the magnifier icon in the top bar to open the search.
3. Type `Artboard`.
4. Press **Down Arrow** or **Up Arrow**.
5. Observe that the highlighted result does not change.

## Why this matters

- A command search is mainly used from the keyboard. Having to reach for the mouse after typing slows users down.
- Arrow key + Enter navigation is the standard behavior in command palettes and search menus (e.g. VS Code, Illustrator, Figma).
- It is also an accessibility issue for users who cannot or prefer not to use a mouse.

- Keep a "selected index" state in the search results list.

title: Allow creating custom standalone (floating) toolbars like Illustrator
author: delit
body:
## Summary

It is currently not possible to create a **custom, standalone toolbar** in Vectorcraft. Users should be able to create one or more new toolbars, pick which tools go into them, and place them freely on the screen (floating or docked). This lets everyone build a compact toolbar with just the tools and shortcuts they use most.

## Current behavior

- Vectorcraft only has the default toolbar.
- There is no way to create a new toolbar, choose which tools it contains, or let it float independently of the main toolbar.
- Users who only need a handful of tools still have to work with the full toolbar or jump between tool groups.

## Expected behavior

Users should be able to:

- [ ] Create a **new toolbar** from a menu (e.g. *New Toolbar...*)
- [ ] Give the toolbar a **name**
- [ ] Choose which **tools and shortcuts** are in it, for example by dragging them from an "All Tools" panel
- [ ] Place the toolbar **freely on the screen** (floating) or dock it

- [ ] Have custom toolbars **saved in the workspace** so they come back when switching workspace (see also the workspace issue about remembering panel widths)

## Reference: how Adobe Illustrator does it

Illustrator has a toolbar menu with the options **Advanced**, **Basic**, **Getting Started**, **New Toolbar...** and **Manage Toolbars...**. An "All Tools" panel lists every tool, grouped by category, and tools can be dragged into a new toolbar. The result is a small floating toolbar with only the chosen tools (see screenshots).

## Why this matters

- Users can build a toolbar tailored to their own workflow, for example one for drawing, one for editing paths, one for text.
- Frequently used tools become one click away, without digging through tool groups.

title: Intertwine is missing: make overlapping objects pass over and under each other
author: delit
body:
## Summary

Vectorcraft has no **Intertwine** feature at all. Intertwine lets the user make overlapping objects look woven together, so one object passes *over* another in one overlap area and *under* it in the next, without permanently changing the objects. It is commonly used for interlocking logos, rings, knots, Celtic-style patterns, ribbons and lettering with overlapping strokes.

## Current behavior

- There is no Intertwine command anywhere in the Object menu or the command search.
- The only workaround is to manually duplicate objects, cut them apart, and rearrange the stacking order. This is slow and destructive, and breaks as soon as a shape is edited.

## Expected behavior

A non-destructive Intertwine workflow, following Illustrator's `Object > Intertwine`:

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Make** | Turns the selected overlapping objects into an *Intertwine group* (shown as a group in the Layers panel). Additional objects can be dragged into the group later. |
| **Edit** | Re-enters the Intertwine group so the intertwined areas can be changed. |
| **Release** | Restores the objects to their original state and removes the Intertwine group. |

Choosing the overlap areas:

- [ ] **Hover/click** an overlapping area to intertwine it
- [ ] **Draw an enclosed path** around an overlapping area (or around an area where three or more objects overlap) to intertwine it
- [ ] The path of the object nearest to the pointer is **highlighted** while hovering, so it is clear which object will go on top

Supported objects:

- [ ] Shapes and paths
- [ ] Text
- [ ] Ideally 2D and 3D objects, if Vectorcraft supports them

Limitations (same as Illustrator, acceptable for a first version):

- Nested Intertwine groups are not supported
- Objects already inside an Intertwine group cannot be used to create a new one
- Not supported together with Live Paint, Repeat or graphs

## Reference

Adobe documentation: [Intertwine objects](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/inter…

title: Two geometry tests fail on macOS x86_64 (pass on FreeBSD CI)
author: ham9zah
body:
Two geometry tests fail on `main` (0d0ea352) on my macOS x86_64 machine: one in `vectorcraft-engine` and one in `vectorcraft-pathops`. The FreeBSD CI job passes on the same commit, and no CI job runs the tests on macOS, so this may be a platform difference (floating-point details) rather than a bug in `main`. I only ran them on this one machine.

## 1. `tests_build::shape_builder_merges_rosette_rings_cleanly`

In `crates/engine/src/tests_build.rs` (see #569).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft
cd vectorcraft
git checkout 0d0ea352
cargo test -p vectorcraft-engine --lib shape_builder_merges_rosette_rings_cleanly
```

```
thread 'tests_build::shape_builder_merges_rosette_rings_cleanly' panicked at crates/engine/src/tests_build.rs:1110:13:
NodeId(65) has an outline 0.778 pt wide on average, 102.8 pt long
```

This is the "no outline is a sliver or carries a spur" check: one outline of the selection is 0.778 pt wide on average, the test wants more than 1.0 pt. It fails the same way at 504e7192, where I first saw it.

## 2. `every_pathfinder_operation_is_pinned`

In `crates/pathops/tests/pathfinder_pinned.rs`.

```sh
git checkout 0d0ea352
cargo test -p vectorcraft-pathops --test pathfinder_pinned
```

```
thread 'every_pathfinder_operation_is_pinned' panicked at crates/pathops/tests/pathfinder_pinned.rs:49:5:
assertion `left == right` failed
```

One of the 40 pinned hashes differs: entry 10 (0-based; the Unite of the 5 shapes, seed 7). It is computed here as `60181664961792917`, the pinned value is `9388160212451732406`; the other 39 match. The hashes are taken over the `{:?}` output of the resulting paths, so a last-bit difference in a coordinate changes it.

Both tests fail every time, alone and in `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (6070 pass, these two fail; that run was without `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`).

title: AI import: global process CMYK swatch read as spot with wrong values; PDF export renders it near-black
author: drumanshoo
body:
## Summary
Opening an Illustrator `.ai` file, a global **process** CMYK swatch is imported as a **spot** colour with the wrong CMYK values. Exporting to PDF then writes a `/Separation` whose alternate colour is that wrong value, so the swatch renders near-black in any PDF viewer. PNG and SVG exports of the same file look correct, so the problem is easy to miss.

## Version / platform
VectorCraft 0.10.0 (`vectorcraft-cli 0.10.0`), Windows 11 x64, portable build.

## What happens
The source file is a client logo saved by Illustrator (PDF-compatible `.ai`, PDF 1.6). I can't post it publicly. Its XMP swatch metadata defines the swatch as:

```xml
<xmpG:swatchName>PMS3538 CP C=93 M=10 Y=0 K=0</xmpG:swatchName>
<xmpG:type>PROCESS</xmpG:type>
<xmpG:mode>CMYK</xmpG:mode>
<xmpG:cyan>93.000001</xmpG:cyan>
<xmpG:magenta>10.000000</xmpG:magenta>
<xmpG:yellow>0.000000</xmpG:yellow>
<xmpG:black>0.000000</xmpG:black>
```

`vectorcraft-cli run --in logo.ai --cmd swatch.list` reports:

```json
{"name": "PMS3538 CP C=93 M=10 Y=0 K=0", "spot": true, "global": true,
 "color": {"model": "cmyk", "c": 1.0, "m": 1.0, "y": 0.0, "k": 0.93}, "hex": "#171426"}
```

So it is marked `spot: true` (the source says PROCESS), and the values look shuffled or clamped (expected c=0.93 m=0.10 y=0 k=0).

`vectorcraft-cli convert logo.ai logo.pdf` then writes:

```
/Separation/PMS3538#20CP#20C=93#20M=10#20Y=0#20K=0/DeviceCMYK<</FunctionType 2/Domain[0 1]/Range[0 1 0 1 0 1 0 1]/C0[0 0 0 0]/C1[1 1 0 0.92941177]/N 1>>
```

Poppler (`pdftoppm`) and PdfCraft both render that area as about `#03030c` / `#000017` (near-black) where the logo is cyan. `convert logo.ai logo.png` and `logo.svg` render the cyan correctly (about `#009be5`).

## Expected
The swatch is imported as a process colour, C=93 M=10 Y=0 K=0, and the PDF renders it cyan.

## Notes
- I couldn't reproduce this with a hand-made PDF carrying the same XMP swatch block, or with a plain `/Separation` (both exported correctly). The wrong values seem to c…

title: [Feature Request] [VectorCraft] Contextual Skew / Shear Cursor on Bounding Box Hover (Quality of Life)
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

Currently, performing a simple tilt or shear (inclination) on an object requires switching to a dedicated transformation tool or manually entering values in a transform panel. 

I propose adding a direct canvas shear gesture using the default Selection Tool, similar to the behavior in Affinity Designer. This allows users to skew objects dynamically without interrupting their workflow to switch tools.

Proposed Behavior & Interaction:

1. Activation:
   - Select any object using the standard Selection Tool.
   - Position the mouse pointer slightly outside the bounding box edge (between two edge/corner handles).

2. Cursor Change:
   - The cursor dynamically changes into a two-way opposing arrows icon (up/down arrows for vertical edges, or left/right arrows for horizontal edges), signaling that a shear action is available.

3. Execution:
   - Click and drag along the edge:
     * Dragging up/down along a vertical edge skews the object vertically.
     * Dragging left/right along a horizontal edge skews the object horizontally.

Key Benefits:
- Time-saving: Eliminates constant tool-switching or panel navigation for minor text/shape tilt adjustments.
- Intuitive UX: Follows well-established vector editing standards, making canvas interactions smoother and more fluid.

title: Fonts: a classic Mac TrueType whose cmap has no Unicode subtable is listed, but every character is missing (and an ideographic space sets at zero width)
author: imachus
body:
### What happens

Some classic Mac TrueType fonts (suitcase files: an empty data fork, the `sfnt` in the resource fork) carry only Macintosh cmap subtables: `(1, 0)` format 0 and `(1, 1)` format 2 (Mac Japanese, i.e. Shift-JIS). I have several of these in a font folder (old DynaFont and Ricoh HG families, sold that way in the 2000s). The scan reads them and lists them in the font menus by their names — but no character maps:

- `text.fonts` reports every character as missing: on a newsletter of 348 distinct characters set in one of them, `missingGlyphs` is 347 (the one exception is U+3000, see below). Kana, kanji, and in these fonts even ASCII digits and letters.
- The type still draws, because each missing glyph is drawn in the fallback font — so the font looks as if it worked, only in the wrong face.
- An ideographic space (U+3000) is the exception: whitespace counts as covered by the primary font (`crates/text/src/shape.rs`, `let covered = c.is_whitespace() || …`), so it isn't sent to the fallback. It's laid out with glyph 0's advance, which is 0 in these fonts, and paragraph indents vanish. For comparison, in Times New Roman, which also lacks U+3000, `あ　あ` measures 3 em; in one of these fonts it measures 2 em.

### Why

`skrifa`'s `Charmap` picks a Unicode subtable, else the Windows symbol one, else Mac Roman `(1, 0)`. With no Unicode subtable, every lookup goes through the Mac Roman table, which in these fonts maps (almost) nothing. The Mac Japanese subtable (format 2) is never read, and reading it would need a Shift-JIS → Unicode table, which the crate doesn't have.

### To reproduce without these fonts

Take any TrueType the tests use, drop every cmap subtable except a `(1, 0)` format 0 one (or keep only a `(1, 1)` format 2 one), wrap it in a resource fork with `suitcase::fork_of` and put it in a scanned folder as a suitcase (empty data fork). It's listed by name; `text.create` with it gives `missingGlyphs` = every non-space character; `あ　あ` measures 2 em ins…
